turns.prompt:
You are given one attached CSV file:
  - cdft_piezo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose
    properties are NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar`
    (the crystal structure, in POSCAR format).

No property values are provided. Using your knowledge of crystal chemistry,
crystal symmetry and structure-property relationships, select the 5
candidates with the LARGEST piezoelectric strain coefficient max|d_ij| (in
pC/N) that also satisfy a low-leakage requirement: the band gap must be at
least 5 eV. Band gaps are NOT given for the pool -- you must infer them. A
selected candidate whose band gap is below the threshold scores zero.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The pool must be filtered first by the two hard requirements (non-centrosymmetric crystal enabling a non-zero piezoelectric tensor, and a chemically inferred gap \(\ge 5\,\mathrm{eV}\)). Half-Heuslers, zinc-blende/wurtzite chalcogenides and pnictides, Bi/Pb/Sb/Te/Ti/Ta compounds and all molecular elemental crystals fail the gap cut. This leaves only highly ionic fluorides, selected chlorides, Be/Al/Si/P oxides, and saline hydrides/hydroxides.

Among the survivors the magnitude of \(\max|d_{ij}|\) is controlled by the usual relation \(d\sim e/C\). The piezoelectric stress \(e\) is modest and comparable for all of these ionic compounds, so the ranking is set by elastic softness and by proximity to a polar instability:

- KCaCl\(_3\) (c011) is a 1-formula-unit perovskite whose cell is only a few degrees and \(\sim 0.2\,\text{Å}\) away from cubic. The polar mode is therefore extremely soft, \(C\) is that of a chloride (\(\sim 30\,\mathrm{GPa}\)) and \(d_{ij}\) is expected to be the largest in the pool.
- The saline hydrides CaAlH\(_5\) (c087) and BeAlH\(_5\) (c084) have still lower moduli (\(20{-}40\,\mathrm{GPa}\)) and polar (or easily polarizable) structures; they rank next.
- Be(OH)\(_2\) (c079) is a polar hydroxide, mechanically intermediate between hydrides and oxides.
- The phosphate K\(_2\)SrP\(_4\)O\(_{12}\) (c005) is a low-symmetry, non-centrosymmetric oxide network whose gap is safely above 5 eV; it is stiffer than the hydrides/chlorides and therefore last of the five.

All other chemically admissible candidates (cubic NaClO\(_3\), gehlenite, orthocarbonates, etc.) are either non-polar or mechanically stiffer and cannot overtake the five listed above.

Final: c011, c087, c084, c079, c005
